The technology issues began on the morning of Oct. 27 [see “CSX operations affected …,” Trains.com, Oct. 28, 2026]. While dispatching and positive train control were not affected, other systems — ranging from crew calling to the ability to exchange interchange data with other railroads — were disrupted, significantly limiting operations. candidates.title: Port of Los Angeles surpasses 1 million TEUs for second consecutive month
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,026,872 TEUs in October 2026, setting a new record for the month. The figure also represents the second-highest monthly container volume in the port’s history. For the first time, the port exceeded 1 million TEUs in two consecutive months. The October performance followed September’s all-time record of 1,042,652 TEUs, marking another milestone for the busiest container port in the United States. The port has now surpassed 1 million TEUs three times in 2026. Furthermore, container throughput between June and October reached nearly 5 million TEUs, the strongest five-month period in its history. Port of Los Angeles Executive Director Gene Seroka attributed the sustained activity to consumer spending, inventory replenishment and changes in trade policy. Ongoing disruptions along other global shipping routes have also influenced cargo movements. The initiative builds on earlier security investments, including a dedicated customs facility and Sweden’s first permanent cargo scanner. SCR is intended to address security risks associated with traditional container release procedures, particularly the sharing of manual release references across logistics chains. candidates.title: From ocean liner to artificial reef: A warning for container shipping
candidates.excerpt: From ocean liner to artificial reef: A warning for container shipping Dr Raymon Krishnan, president of Singapore’s Logistics & Supply Chain Management Society, writes for Splash today, reflecting on one of this week’s most talked about stories in the mainstream press. On Wednesday, the 990-foot ocean liner SS United States was deliberately sunk off Destin, Florida, to become what is expected to be the world’s largest artificial reef. Initial underwater inspections found the vessel upright, approximately 180 feet below the surface. The sinking of the SS United States reminds us that ships can outlive their commercial purpose. Launched in 1951 and entering service in 1952, the SS United States was the pinnacle of post-war American maritime engineering. It held the record as the world’s fastest passenger ship but was withdrawn in 1969 as commercial aviation transformed the economics of transatlantic travel. candidates.excerpt: New report identifies Hong Kong’s place in world shipping Hong Kong Maritime Week is about to kick off. To celebrate the occasion, Splash today publishes a 48-page magazine on the city’s maritime hub credentials. A ship can be ordered at a mainland Chinese yard, owned through a leasing company in Hong Kong, insured in London, crewed through a management operation in Asia and chartered from Singapore. Its cargo need never pass through Hong Kong’s harbour. Even its Hong Kong financing vehicle may have to seek credit approval elsewhere. The geography of shipping has always been complicated. Metallic ores and metals followed with a 6.4% increase. Grain shipments declined 2.4%, nonmetallic minerals fell 1.7%, and coal slipped 1.2% among weaker volumes. candidates.title: Illinois Railway Museum acquires ex-Burlington bilevel gallery cars
candidates.excerpt: UNION, Ill. — The Illinois Railway Museum (IRM) has acquired a second complete and operational train of bilevel gallery cars, this one from the former Chicago, Burlington & Quincy Railroad. The stainless-steel consist of two coaches and a cab car arrived at the museum grounds on Wednesday night (Nov. 11), having spent approximately the last 20 years in Michigan. Coaches Nos. 702 and 709 were built by Budd in 1950 and were among the first gallery cars constructed. They were revolutionary, according to IRM. The Burlington’s new fleet offered air conditioning, sealed windows, and comfortable seats. The two-level design also permitted higher seating capacity, while the open gallery down the middle allowed conductors to collect fares from both levels simultaneously. candidates.excerpt: BNSF’s third-quarter earnings rose 19.3% to $1.73 billion as higher freight volumes and improved operating efficiencies helped offset increased fuel costs. The railroad’s net earnings increased from $1.45 billion in the third quarter of 2025, parent company Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK-B) reported. Railroad operating revenue climbed 14.7% to $6.87 billion, while car and unit volumes rose 3.9%, for the period ended Sept. 30. The results extended BNSF’s earnings growth for the year. Through September, net earnings reached $4.66 billion, up 13% from $4.13 billion in the first nine months of 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,883 carloads, to 25,059; chemicals, up 2,542 carloads, to 34,523; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,351 carloads, to 16,268.
